# okfs 0.1.0

The first full release. okfs is an open-source web file browser in one binary: run it in a folder and flip through every file with the keyboard, each one shown beside the list as the cursor lands on it.

Try it in your browser: https://okfs.jrnxf.co/demo/

## Install

```sh
brew install jrnxf/tap/okfs
docker run -p 8080:8080 -v "$PWD:/srv:ro" ghcr.io/jrnxf/okfs
nix run github:jrnxf/okfs
cargo install --git https://github.com/jrnxf/okfs   # needs Rust and bun
```

Archives for Linux (x86-64 and arm64, static), macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Windows (x86-64) are below, each with a `.sha256`. [docs/install.md](https://github.com/jrnxf/okfs/blob/main/docs/install.md) has a `curl` download with the checksum step.

## What is in it

- Previews for images, video, audio, PDF, Markdown, source code, CSV, JSON, zip files and HTML pages, shown beside the list as the cursor moves. Hold `j` and each file shows as the cursor passes it.
- Columns for the folder under the cursor.
- A palette (`Ctrl K`) that searches every name in the tree.
- The page follows the folder as files change.
- Eleven themes, each one CSS file.
- Loopback and read only by default. Beyond loopback, a key in the link, and optional HTTPS. `--allow-upload`, `--allow-edit` and `--allow-delete` are separate flags, with a 30-day Trash.

## What you can rely on from this version

The flags, the `OKFS_*` variables, the exit codes and the addresses under "Addresses you can rely on" in [docs/usage.md](https://github.com/jrnxf/okfs/blob/main/docs/usage.md#what-you-can-rely-on). Everything under `/api/`, what okfs prints in the terminal and the Rust library may change in any release.

## Known limits

- No accounts. The key is one shared secret, new at every start.
- No base path: behind a proxy, okfs needs a host name of its own.
- The binaries are not signed, so macOS and Windows warn about one that a browser downloaded. [docs/install.md](https://github.com/jrnxf/okfs/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the way around it.
- The Windows build is new and lightly tested.
- okfs has had no outside security review. [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jrnxf/okfs/blob/main/SECURITY.md) says how to report a fault.
